gameFeelChanges: Every take/undo acorn button now has tactile press feedback (scale .86 on :active) and pops in with a spring easing when it appears in the tree/basket pile (.tree-pile .interaction, .basket-pile .interaction — new @keyframes pop-in, 0.32s).
Guide bear icon (top-left) has a very subtle idle breathing animation (idle-breathe, 2.6s loop) so the scene doesn't feel static while waiting for input.
Each waiting friend card bobs gently (idle-bob, staggered per friend) instead of sitting frozen.
Success and chapter-result cards now pop in with a spring animation (card-pop) instead of appearing instantly.

Chapter-end celebration ('bloom') redesigned: was a plain dotted orange circle — now a glowing circle with a flower emoji and an 8-dot CSS confetti burst (bloom-pop + confetti-burst keyframes). This is the biggest 'feels like a game, not a worksheet' change.
All new animations are covered by the existing global prefers-reduced-motion:reduce rule (already present in mission.css, disables all animation/transition site-wide) — nothing new bypasses it.
No change to timing logic, scoring, state machine, or any of the five teaching rules in LEARNING-DESIGN.md — purely presentational.

structuralChanges3rdRound.trigger: User explicitly pushed back that the whole redesign still read as a worksheet with no journey/story ('길가다 나무발견하고 그런 스토리도없고... 학습지 풀듯 문제나오고'), after rounds 1-2 had only reskinned assets + added micro-animation juice onto the exact same linear scene-swap flow. User was asked to scope the fix (AskUserQuestion) and chose full structural redesign (overworld/map), not just a light narrative wrapper.
whatChanged: New 'overworld' screen (showMap() in mission.js): a vertical forest-path map with one node per concept (share/compare/make), using CONCEPTS[].name/short fields that already existed in the code but were never surfaced in the UI before. Nodes show locked/current/done state with a progress checkmark; locked nodes are inert, current/done nodes are clickable to travel there.

New 'travel' screen (travelBeat() in mission.js): a short one-line discovery beat ('오솔길을 따라 걷다 보니, 배고픈 친구들이 나무 아래 모여 있어요!' etc, one line per concept in TRAVEL_LINES) shown once per chapter, between the demo step and the first real task — replaces the previous instant demo->task cut with an actual 'arriving somewhere' moment.

Navigation rewiring only: 'start' now opens the map instead of jumping straight into chapter 1; 'next-chapter' (chapter-end button) now returns to the map instead of auto-advancing to the next chapter, so the player chooses the next node themselves; a new 'unlocked' counter on the persistent state object tracks map progress. 'repeat' (replay same chapter) is unchanged.

ZERO changes to feedback()/assess()/advance()/the take|undo|submit|choose branches of handle() — scoring, probe/transfer independence tracking, hint logic, and the five teaching rules in LEARNING-DESIGN.md are byte-for-byte untouched. Only presentation-layer entry points (showIntro/chapterEnd's button routing, demo's continue button) got new intermediate screens inserted around them.
structuralChanges3rdRound.verification: Full Playwright run-through of all 3 concepts end-to-end (share -> compare -> make) via the game's own exposed __moaMissionQA() state readout, confirming: map unlock progression (locked -> current -> done) after each chapter, zero console/page errors across the whole run, clicking a 'done' map node correctly replays that chapter from its demo step, and the pre-existing early-mastery-exit rule in advance() (skipping remaining practice items once criteria are met) still fires exactly as before — confirming no scoring-path regression.
